_doc: Curated critical-package map for Security's security_patch_scan (stage 1). Each family describes WHAT the component is, its system blast radius, and the post-update action. It carries NO vulnerability/CVE severity - that is stage 2 (Ubuntu Security Notices / CVE correlation). component_criticality is blast-radius (how much of the system the component touches), which is evidence, not an inferred vulnerability score. A package matches a family if its name is in `names` or starts with one of `prefixes`.

glibc.label: GNU C Library (glibc)
glibc.what_it_is: The GNU C library - the standard C library linked by virtually every binary and every Python process on the host, including all MycOS agents and services.
glibc.system_impact: A patch here touches the whole system. Running processes keep the old library mapped in memory until they are restarted, so applying the update does not protect a process that is already running.
glibc.post_update_action: After applying, restart the MycOS agents in the venv so they run on the patched library. No reboot is required unless the reboot flag is set.

openssl.label: OpenSSL / libssl
openssl.what_it_is: The TLS/crypto library behind HTTPS, certificate verification and secure connections.
openssl.system_impact: Every agent making outbound HTTPS calls (CourtListener, web search, model APIs) and any TLS listener depends on it. A flaw can mean breakable or forgeable encryption on exactly the connections that carry sensitive data.
openssl.post_update_action: Restart any service holding long-lived TLS connections after applying. No reboot required unless the reboot flag is set.

kernel.label: Linux kernel
kernel.system_impact: A kernel update is the one case that requires a REBOOT to take effect; until the reboot the running kernel is unchanged and unprotected. The phase-1 Docker sandbox shares this kernel, so a kernel flaw is also a container-isolation concern.
kernel.post_update_action: Schedule a reboot - nothing picks up a kernel patch without one. The reboot flag will usually confirm this.

openssh.label: OpenSSH
openssh.what_it_is: The SSH client and server - remote login and file transfer for this host.
openssh.system_impact: openssh-server is the remote-access surface reachable directly from the network, so a flaw here is among the most exposed. openssh-client affects outbound SSH (e.g. git over SSH).
openssh.post_update_action: Restart the ssh service after applying (sudo systemctl restart ssh); existing sessions stay up. No reboot required.

docker.label: Docker / containerd
docker.what_it_is: The container engine, CLI and build tooling.
docker.system_impact: The phase-1 agent sandbox and Jellyfin run on Docker. Restarting the daemon to apply an engine update bounces every running container.
docker.post_update_action: Apply during a maintenance window - restarting Docker will restart running containers (Jellyfin, any sandboxed agents). No host reboot required.
